Phase 1: Mental Models & Local Cluster Setup (Week 1)Start by understanding why container orchestration exists and how a control plane coordinates worker nodes. Spin up a lightweight local cluster so you can inspect resources safely.   What to learn: Containers vs. Pods, control plane components (API server, etcd, scheduler, controller manager), worker nodes (kubelet, kube-proxy, container runtime), declarative YAML manifests, and basic kubectl commands (get, describe, logs, apply).   YouTube Videos:Kubernetes Roadmap - Complete Step-by-Step Learning Path — Good for mapping out terminology and sequence before watching long deep-dives.   Kubernetes Tutorial for Beginners [FULL COURSE in 4 Hours] — Classic visual walkthrough of core objects, architecture, Minikube setup, and YAML basics.   Online Resources:Kubernetes Official Documentation — Concepts & Tutorials — Read the Components of a Cluster and Workloads and Pods pages alongside your videos.   Killercoda Interactive Environments — Browser-based sandboxes so you can practice kubectl immediately without heavy local VM overhead.Phase 2: Workloads, Configuration & Networking (Weeks 2–3)Once you can run a single Pod, move to managing lifecycle, externalizing configuration, and routing traffic cleanly inside and outside the cluster.What to learn: ReplicaSet and Deployment rollouts/rollbacks, ConfigMap and Secret, ClusterIP / NodePort / LoadBalancer Services, DNS resolution, and ingress/routing (Ingress and Gateway API).   YouTube Videos:The Kubernetes Course 2025 — Strong end-to-end breakdown covering architecture, kube-proxy, CoreDNS, Deployments, ConfigMaps/Secrets, Services, and Gateway API.   Kubernetes Tutorial: From Zero to Deployed (100% FREE) — Concise walkthrough taking a basic deployment through scaling, self-healing, and Kustomize.   Online Resources:Kubernetes Official Tutorials — Try the stateless application and Service exposure walkthroughs.   Phase 3: State, Storage, Security & Packaging (Weeks 4–5)Stateless apps are straightforward; real-world workloads require persistent state, least-privilege access, and repeatable deployments.What to learn: Volumes, PersistentVolume (PV), PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC), StorageClass, StatefulSet, RBAC (roles, role bindings, service accounts), and templating/packaging with Helm or Kustomize.   YouTube Videos:Certified Kubernetes Administrator Exam Preparation (2026 Update) — Structured modules covering RBAC, Helm/Kustomize, autoscaling, PV/PVC/StorageClasses, and practical troubleshooting workflows.   Phase 4: Troubleshooting & Capstone Deployment (Week 6+)The fastest way to cement Kubernetes knowledge is breaking things intentionally and deploying a multi-component app.What to learn: Debugging CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, Pending pods, service endpoint mismatches, resource limits/requests, and basic cluster observability (metrics and logs).   Practice Goal: Deploy a small multi-service app (API + worker + database/cache) using declarative manifests or Helm, expose an endpoint, inspect logs/events when something fails, and tear it down cleanly.
